_provenance.rule: Every last price is the 'FEED: <ticker> last $<price>' figure from the dataset prose. Order limits in the dataset are deliberately NOT stored here: limits belong to the order request, not to the market.
notes: AAPL 188.97 (cases 01, 06), SPY 499.84 (cases 02, 03), MSFT 89.95 (cases 04, 05, 10), AMZN 998.12 (case 07), GOOG 239.71 and GOOGL 168.20 (case 08), BTC-USD 62995.00 (case 09).

GOOG is present because the dataset's case 08 quotes it, even though it is NOT on the instrument allowlist. Fetching a quote for a ticker and being allowed to TRADE that ticker are different questions, and the policy kernel answers the second one.

Case 11 needs AAPL under an LULD volatility circuit breaker, while cases 01 and 06 need AAPL trading normally. A single fixture cannot be both, so each ticker carries a `snapshots` map: `default` is the ordinary feed, `halted` is the halted feed. get_market_quote returns `default` unless the caller asks for another snapshot, which keeps the default view consistent with the majority of cases.
asOf is a fixed historical timestamp on purpose: the fixture must not change between runs.

GOOGL is quoted at two different prices in the dataset (168.20 in case 08, 159.90 in case 12). The default snapshot carries the case-08 print and the case-12 print is recorded under alternatePrints, so the conflict is visible instead of hidden.

GOOG.note: Real ticker, NOT on the instrument allowlist: GOOG is not GOOGL.

alternatePrints.note: The dataset quotes GOOGL twice at different prices: 168.20 in case 08 and 159.90 in case 12. Rather than pick one and hide the other, the second print is recorded here. get_market_quote returns the default snapshot; a caller that needs the other print has the same limit as the dataset had, and no tool invents a merge.

BTC-USD.note: Crypto pair: never on the instrument allowlist, however reasonable the size.

allowlistMatch: exact-string match on the ticker symbol
